item.title: [New] Out-of-band security updates for .NET, ASP.NET Core, PowerShell 7.4/7.6 and Visual Studio: the October Scan Cab was reissued on 25 October, so offline compliance scans run before then miss them
item.description:
Two remote code execution fixes outside Patch Tuesday land in runtimes that sit on web servers and admin hosts (ASP.NET Core, PowerShell 7). An offline or WSUS-scan-cab compliance report taken with the earlier cab shows these hosts as compliant while they are not.

Windows · Redeploy the reissued wsusscn2.cab wherever offline scans are used, then find hosts running .NET 8/9/10, ASP.NET Core, PowerShell 7.4/7.6 or Visual Studio in Defender Vulnerability Management and patch internet-facing ASP.NET Core servers first.

item.title: [New] KMS Hardware-Secured: KMS hosts will have to prove their hardware with TPM attestation before activating clients, mandatory from the next Windows Server LTSC
item.description:
Rogue KMS hosts are a known way to activate untrusted machines inside a network; KMS hosts on hardware without TPM attestation will stop qualifying with the next LTSC.

Windows Server · Inventory KMS hosts (DNS _vlmcs SRV records), check slmgr /dlv and the Key Management Service event log for readiness warnings, and run the Key Attestation check on physical hosts.

item.title: [New] CVE-2026-102204 (WSL elevation of privilege) now names Windows Subsystem for Linux as the affected product; update WSL to the latest version
item.description:
WSL updates through the Store or wsl --update, not Windows Update, so a host fully patched by Windows Update can still run the vulnerable WSL.

Windows · Query the WSL version across developer endpoints (wsl --version, or DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory) and push wsl --update where it lags.

item.title: [New] Quick machine recovery reaches Windows Server 2025 with the October 2026 security update, switched off by default
item.description:
Enabled, the feature lets a server that cannot boot fetch and apply a remediation from Windows Update before the OS starts, which is a change-control and evidence question on domain controllers and other tier-0 servers; nothing changes until the policy is turned on.

Windows Server · Decide per server class whether quick machine recovery may be enabled; if you enable it, exclude or explicitly approve domain controllers and record the Group Policy setting in your baseline. Confirm in your own tenant.
